reviews.title: Manual Macro Targets?
reviews.text:
“Food, [Macro], & Fitness Tracker”.

For an app that advertises itself as a macro tracker, you’d expect yourself to be able to manually enter your macro targets - right? 

Wrong!

In this (paid for) app you have to choose percentages of your target calorie goal for the app to pick the individual macros for you. You’d expect such a simple little function to be available through this app.

I swapped from a different calorie tracker (ProCal) to give this one a shot because it was slightly cheaper (still $30) after the free trial. I guess in the end you get what you pay for, but overall if you care about tracking your macros as close as possible, I’d recommend a different tracker unless they add this function.

reviews.title: Buggy as hell
reviews.text:
I’ve been using this app for over a year and it has a lot of potential, but it’s currently held back by several frustrating bugs and poor design decisions that make daily use much more annoying than it needs to be.
Major Issues:
•  History & Search is broken: The recent items/history shows random old entries from over a year ago instead of prioritizing what I actually use. The search function doesn’t update live — you have to hit enter every time. Results appear in seemingly random order with no logic based on frequency of use. For example, I eat the same Costco salmon snack almost every weekday, yet it’s never near the top and I have to dig through the list every single time.
•  Frequent freezing in menus: When navigating multiple levels deep (especially when editing custom foods or meals), the app regularly freezes and stops responding to any input. The only fix is to force-close and restart the app, which means losing whatever information you were entering. This happens way too often.
•  Custom meals are poorly handled: When you create a custom meal (like a 32-ingredient smoothie), it saves everything as individual line items instead of keeping them grouped as one meal. If you accidentally assign it to the wrong meal time, you have to swipe and delete every single ingredient manually. This feels like a basic design oversight.
•  Dangerous Health app integration: By default, the app pulls activity data from Apple Health and automatically adds calories back to your daily tot

reviews.title: good app, just a few issues
reviews.text:
Hello! I like appediet alot personally. It's totally free to use, and it's super convenient. All the basic features don't require a subscription, so you can use it for free. I haven't tried the food scan feature, I always input the food I eat manually, but l've never had any issues with it. :)
There's one thing I'd like to criticise, and it's about weight stigmatising. For context, l've struggled with food and been severely underweight in the past.
The issue I have with appediet is the subtle suggestion that gaining weight is bad. When you track your weight in this app, any weight loss will show a green arrow (implying good), and weight gain will show a red arrow (implying bad). I also got a notification this morning that said something like, "Make sure to track your diet today so you don't overeat." I understand appediet is marketed as a weight loss app (not weight gain), and thats totally fine! it's really not a huge deal, but these small details insinuate that weight gain is bad, and its not always. There are healthy ways to gain weight, which can be beneficial for cases like mine :)

edit: im changing this review because i no longer agree with this use of ai and data collection. i think ai should not be so normalized either, please reconsider supporting apps like this, especially big companies
